clue.text: Naughty bits apt to make one religious

indicators.note: naughty things misbehave and will not stay in line, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the two words taken as written, seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A cheeky hint that something rude could, oddly, turn a person to faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Naughty bits' reads as a coy phrase for private parts, but 'Naughty' alone is the signal and 'bits apt' is the raw material.
explanation.definitionFit: A Baptist is a member of a Protestant church practising adult immersion, so a believer of a particular denomination.

clue.text: Part of team at Euros but not getting paid

indicators.note: a part of something is a piece lying inside it, so the letters sit within the following words

blocks.note: found running across the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A footballer in a squad at the European Championships who plays without a salary.
explanation.walkthrough: The Euros is the European football championship; the answer straddles three words of that phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur takes part for love rather than money, receiving no wages or professional fees for the activity.

clue.text: Sycophant is present as duke descends

blocks.note: the present day, now

explanation.surface: A fawning courtier hovers nearby as a duke makes his way downstairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' is a noun meaning now, not a verb or adjective. Moving its D one place further down the column swaps it with the A.
explanation.definitionFit: A toady is someone who flatters and fawns on the powerful to win favour, exactly what a sycophant does.

clue.text: Resolve to take a city

blocks.note: to resolve a dispute is to settle it
taken as written

explanation.surface: An army commander's determination to capture a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resolve' reads as a noun meaning determination; here it is the verb, as in settling an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Seattle is the largest city in Washington State in the north-western United States, an example of a city.

clue.text: Quickly leave launch strip

explanation.walkthrough: 'Launch strip' looks like one phrase, a runway, but it splits into two more meanings, making three in all.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb covers rushing away and undressing, while the noun form names the moment a plane becomes airborne.

clue.text: Nature's mutated when uranium's left behind

clue.text: Premature attempt to acquire recipe for cheaper menu option

clue.text: Her singing is the end

setter's reading: the proverbial figure whose song signals that something is finally over

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'it ain't over till the ___ sings' names an operatic soprano whose aria closes the show.

clue.text: Expose bias on television, where radical thinking may take place

side as in taking sides, partiality
the box is informal British slang for television

explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' places one part above the next. 'The box' is British slang for the television set.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'think outside the box' means thinking unconventionally, beyond the usual limits, so this is the place of original ideas.

clue.text: Shanghai regularly deserted? It's a long story

explanation.walkthrough: 'Deserted' suggests empty streets; with 'regularly' it means the even letters are abandoned.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a lengthy narrative, originally an Icelandic tale of heroes and families, now any long-running tale.

clue.text: What grown-ups pay to acquire drug, being lower in quality

definitions.note: adjective phrase for an adjective sense, debased

indicators.note: to acquire is to take in and hold, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: the full ticket price charged to grown-ups
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: The price adults pay for illegal substances, which tend to be impure.
explanation.walkthrough: E for ecstasy is a common crossword abbreviation; it slots between the two words of the ticket price.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, adulterate means debased or made impure by added inferior substances, so of reduced quality.

clue.text: Crowd can live with hollow victory

indicators.note: something hollow has had its insides removed, so only the outer shell remains

blocks.note: to be is to exist or live
first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Fans are able to accept a win that feels empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hollow victory' looks like a fixed phrase for an empty win; here it means removing the middle of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A bevy is a group or gathering, originally of birds or girls, so a crowd of people.

clue.text: With luck, it covers any parts being displayed

definitions.text: With luck, it covers any parts being displayed

indicators.note: things put on display are arranged afresh, so the letters are set out in a new order

blocks.note: the two words taken as written

explanation.surface: A cosmetic coating that, if you're lucky, reaches all your exposed skin.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, and the last part also supplies the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A fake tan is sprayed onto the body, and the hope is that it evenly colours whatever skin is on show.

clue.text: Build up for goal in free flowing soccer

indicators.note: flowing freely means moving loosely without fixed order, so the letters are reorganised

blocks.note: an end is a goal or aim
taken as written

explanation.surface: A team's attacking moves leading to a goal in fluid, open football.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goal' sounds like a football score, but it means an aim or end, which joins the game's name to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A crescendo is a gradual increase in loudness or intensity, a musical or dramatic building towards a climax.

clue.text: Demanding type of test for fuelless energy

indicators.note: less means without, so a letter is taken away

blocks.note: a stress test checks how something copes under pressure
the word for petrol and the like, minus E, the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A tough engine trial run on an empty tank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fuelless' looks like one word meaning empty; it splits into the word, a minus sign and the energy symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stressful causes strain because it asks a lot of you, so it is taxing or demanding.

clue.text: Recording material introducing video into New York libraries

indicators.note: an introduction is the opening of something, so each word gives only its opening letter

blocks.note: the opening letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: Audio media brought into New York's public libraries alongside films.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Introducing' looks like bringing something in, but it picks the first letters of the words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinyl is the plastic from which gramophone records are pressed, and the word now stands for records themselves.

clue.text: Host is shot when it gets a bit cooler

indicators.note: something shot is knocked out, so the word loses its opening letter and keeps its tail

blocks.note: the little word with its front letter knocked off
what hot becomes when it cools slightly

explanation.surface: A party host is exhausted once the evening finally cools down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host' reads as someone entertaining guests; it is the old sense of a great multitude, as in a heavenly host.
explanation.definitionFit: A host can mean a large number of people or things, and a swarm is a dense moving mass of them.

clue.text: Cope successfully with atmospherics?

blocks.note: first meaning: come through a difficulty, as with a storm
second meaning: atmospheric conditions such as rain and wind

explanation.walkthrough: 'Atmospherics' suggests mood or radio interference; here it means conditions in the atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means survive a hardship intact; as a noun it is the state of the air outside, rain or sunshine.

clue.text: Sedate don goes wild when definitely passed over

indicators.note: running wild means out of control and in disorder, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the two words taken as written

explanation.surface: A calm university lecturer loses his temper on being overlooked for promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passed over' suggests being ignored for promotion; here it means passed over to the other side, that is, died.
explanation.definitionFit: Stone dead means completely and unquestionably dead, so certainly having passed away.

clue.text: Particle has complicated route between two points

indicators.note: something complicated is tangled up, so the letters are muddled into a new order
lying between things means sitting inside them, flanked on each side

blocks.note: taken as written
two compass points, north and north

explanation.surface: A subatomic particle takes a winding path from one point to another.
explanation.walkthrough: Compass points supply N, E, S or W; here both are N, wrapped round the reworked word.
explanation.definitionFit: A neutron is an uncharged subatomic particle found in the nucleus of every atom except ordinary hydrogen.

clue.text: Press more air out

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or wrong, so the letters are put in another arrangement

blocks.note: the two words taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to squeeze extra air from something, like a pump or cushion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' looks like a verb; it is a noun, an old word for a cupboard for linen or clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A press is a large cupboard for clothes or linen, and an armoire is such a tall wardrobe.

clue.text: Creep removes both names from rave report

indicators.note: to remove is to take away, so the named letters vanish

blocks.note: to rave is to rant
a report is a loud bang, as of a gun
N is the abbreviation for name, taken twice

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rave report' looks like a glowing review; it is two separate words, each losing one N.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratbag is informal for a nasty, contemptible person, much like calling someone a creep.

clue.text: Embarrass person of substance when lot includes forgery

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it within, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: one's lot in life is one's fate
a sham is a fake or forgery

explanation.surface: Humiliating a wealthy figure when an auction lot turns out to be fake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Person of substance' suggests a rich or important person; here it means a large person.
explanation.definitionFit: To fat-shame is to mock or humiliate someone for being overweight, a heavier individual in polite euphemism.

clue.text: Great book, in my opinion

definitions.note: read as two words, a phrase rather than a noun

blocks.note: first meaning: a large, heavy volume
second meaning: as I see it, split into a preposition and a pronoun

explanation.surface: A reader's personal verdict that a book is wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great' looks like praise but means large; the second meaning only works when the answer is split as 'to me'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tome is a large, heavy volume, especially a scholarly one, so a big book.

clue.text: Raised bet wins nothing when century scored

blocks.note: a punt is a bet
zero, nothing

clue.text: Imagine writer being one of these Scousers!

clue.text: Gullible senate shifts from the centre
